title: Build a small 3D island adventure game with an agent
summary: A creator had Codex, with a 3D model maker called Tripo plugged in, build a playable island adventure game; they say it took under an hour.
agent_role: The agent built the prototype, used Tripo to generate, rig and animate 3D assets, integrated them, and polished lighting, movement, camera and the finale. The human set the creative brief and directed each phase.
outcome: Author reports the playable game, LUMEN ISLES, was built in under an hour, shown in a video.
what_they_did: The creator asked GPT-6 Astra, working inside Codex, for a small, cozy island adventure. It needed a lighthouse, cottages and lanterns. Tripo, a tool that makes 3D models, was connected to Codex. Astra first built a rough playable version with stand-in shapes. Tripo then made the 3D models and gave the main character a skeleton and animations. Astra fitted it all together and polished the lighting, movement, camera and a lighthouse ending.
how_it_went: The author says the game, LUMEN ISLES, is playable and was made in under an hour. They show it in a video.
worth_knowing: Building a rough playable version with stand-in shapes first, then swapping in the finished models, kept the work simple.
prompt: Using the Tripo CLI connected to this environment, build a small playable 3D game: [describe the world, e.g. a cozy island with a lighthouse and cottages]. First make a working prototype with simple placeholder models and show it to me. Once I approve, use Tripo to generate the 3D assets, rig and animate the main character, and replace the placeholders. Then integrate everything and polish lighting, movement and camera. End with [finale idea]. Summarize what you built and how to run it.

curation.rationale: A clear multi-step workflow combining a coding agent with a 3D-asset CLI to produce a playable game, shown in a demo video. The steps are only lightly detailed.
